title: Larius/Comacinus L.
description: Larius/Comacinus L. (Lake Como). Until the 12th century CE, "Comacinus" was the name commonly used to refer only to the eastern branch of Lake Como—extending from Bellagio south to Brivio—and the surrounding area ("Comacina"). "Larius", "Cumanus", and "Comensis" were the names commonly used to denote the remaining part of Lake Como. After that date, the names "Comacinus", "Cumanus", "Comensis", and "Larius" gradually began to be used interchangeably to refer to the entire lake.
